title: Read every supplier's upload in the charset it was written in

blocks.text: The marketplace imports product lists that suppliers upload. Each supplier declares the charset its file is written in when it signs up: some send UTF-8, a Danish bakery sends ISO-8859-1, and a Dutch gift shop's till exports windows-1252. Since the import went live, the shop shows names like `Sm�rrebr�d kit`, the gift cards' prices have lost their currency sign, and last week an upload that broke off halfway through was imported anyway, with a garbled last line.
`names` already splits the text into product names. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/FeedDecoder.java`:

items: `decode(body, charsetName)`: the text of an upload's body, given the charset its supplier declared. A body that isn't valid text in that charset is refused with a `CharacterCodingException`, so the import skips it and asks the supplier to send it again.

cases.says: an upload declared as UTF-8 yields its product names as the supplier wrote them
an upload declared as ISO-8859-1 keeps its accented letters
an upload that broke off in the middle of a character is refused, not imported
an upload declared as windows-1252 keeps its euro signs

origin.section: Bytes Become Text Only Through a Charset, and new String(bytes) Picks One for You

concepts: Bytes become text only through a charset; new String(bytes) uses the default, UTF-8 since Java 18, so data in another charset must have its charset named.
new String(bytes, charset) silently replaces undecodable bytes with U+FFFD; a CharsetDecoder set to REPORT, or Files.readString, throws instead.
